content.title: How rich is Rory McIlroy? World No 2 wins back-to-back Masters to join Jack Nicklaus, Nick Faldo and Tiger
content.text: Rory McIlroy added another milestone to his career at the Masters on Sunday, breaking clear of the field with two key birdies around Amen Corner. He, as is often the case, left a touch of late tension before sealing the win, etching his name into Augusta National history as only the fourth golfer to defend the title successfully in consecutive years.With another green jacket, McIlroy joined Tiger Woods, Nick Faldo, and Jack Nicklaus as the only repeat winners of the Masters. In a final round where three players had a two-shot lead, McIlroy took control with a bold shot over Rae’s Creek to 7 feet for birdie on the par-3 12th. Then he blistered a 350-yard drive on the par-5 13th that set up another birdie to move three shots ahead.There were a few tense moments along the way including a shot over the par-3 16th green that required him to use the slope to get in close for par, having to get up-and-down for par on the 17th, and a wild drive on the 18th that wound up closer to the 10th fairway. He tapped in for bogey and a 1-under 71 for a one-shot victory over Scottie Scheffler. A year ago, his playoff victory over Justin Rose made McIlroy only the sixth player with the career Grand Slam. McIlroy stood tall when he tapped in the final putt to finish at 12-under 276. It was more heartache for Rose and frustration for the others who had a chance. Rose had a two-shot lead that evaporated around Amen Corner with two bogeys and a three-putt par. He couldn't make up enough ground the rest of the way and had to settle for a third close call at the Masters.Cameron Young lost his two-shot lead much earlier with a long three-putt bogey on the par-3 sixth and taking a bogey on the next hole when he hit a wedge from the fairway into a bunker. One shot behind going to the back nine, Young closed with nine straight pars.Scottie Scheffler, the world No. 1, was in a position to potentially challenge the Masters record for the biggest 36-hole comeback in history. He started the weekend 12 shots back and had cut the deficit to just two strokes as he headed to the turn in the final round.Who is Rory McIlroy? Career and Net WorthRory McIlroy, the 36-year-old from Holywood, Northern Ireland, turned professional in 2007 and joined the PGA TOUR in 2010. He has amassed 29 PGA TOUR victories from 277 starts, with 245 cuts made and career earnings exceeding $110.1 million. Ranked No. 2 in the world (OWGR), McIlroy has collected multiple signature wins, including three in 2025 and a victory at the 2025 Masters Tournament at Augusta National Golf Club, according to the PGA Tour website.ALSO READ: Who is Rory McIlroy married to? Inside how he met wife Erica 14 years ago, filed for divorce, then reconciled within weeksMcIlroy has recorded 29 victories on the PGA TOUR, alongside 13 runner-up finishes and 11 third-place results. He has accumulated 85 top-five finishes and 134 top-10s, reflecting consistent contention at the highest level. Across his career, he has also finished inside the top 25 on 191 occasions, with two withdrawals and no disqualifications recorded. According to Celebrity Net Worth, McIlroy’s net worth is $250 million. With the latest win under his belt, McIlroy secured a Masters-record $4.5 million winner's check. That payout pushed his official PGA TOUR career earnings to a staggering $114,696,641.
